instruction_text: Speak directly to one listener with warmth and a smile in your voice; calm, steady and reassuring, like a favorite morning radio host, while keeping the news clear and credible.
asr_text: It is like someone saying, I won't drive, but helping to put fuel in a car. Not driving is not the same as not helping the trip. But this example cannot tell us who is responsible for military support. We need to check what the words include. So if you say, Britain won't attack, you take what was said about the Typhoon mission too far. You make it sound like it covers all British support. But if you look at the refueling support and say, then the Typhoons will attack too, you claim more than the facts show. The tools for reading news are not a magnifying glass, they are three questions: Who? For which mission? Doing what? Don't stop after seeing the big sign that says to protect. Look at the name tag under it too. Putting one subject back in place can change how the news looks.
